binders: There exist real constants c and C.
Universally quantify over a nonempty finite index type ι, a measurable space Ω, and a probability measure μ on Ω.
Universally quantify over a family X : ι → Ω → Real.
Universally quantify over a real parameter lam.
Define K to be max_i (LocalDef001 μ (X i)).toReal.
hypotheses: The constants satisfy c > 0 and C > 0.
The finite index family is nonempty.
For every i, X i is Borel-measurable.
For every i, X i is μ-integrable and has integral zero.
For every i, LocalDef001 μ (X i) is strictly below infinity in ENNReal.
The family X is mutually independent under μ.
The family maximum K is strictly positive.
conclusions: For every i, ω ↦ exp(lam · X i ω) is μ-integrable.
For every i, ∫ exp(lam · X i) dμ ≤ exp(C · lam² · ((LocalDef001 μ (X i)).toReal)²).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef002 μ X s means that X is measurable, s is an ENNReal scale distinct from zero and infinity, exp(|X|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
LocalDef001 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of all scales s satisfying LocalDef002 μ X s.
K is the nonempty finite maximum of the real-converted LocalDef001 scales of the family.
The small-parameter interval is the symmetric interval |lam| ≤ c/K.
The bound for each variable uses its own scale, not K, in the quadratic exponent C · lam² · scale_i².
translation.proposition_plain_english: There are universal positive real constants c and C such that every nonempty finite mutually independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables with finite exponential-moment scales satisfies the following: if the largest scale K is positive and the real parameter lam obeys |lam| ≤ c/K, then every exponential exp(lam X_i) is integrable and its expectation is at most exp(C lam² times the square of that variable's own scale).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The witnesses c and C are chosen before every index type, probability space, family, and parameter, so both are uniform over all later data.
The index family must be finite and nonempty.
The variables need not be identically distributed; they are required to be mutually independent, individually measurable and integrable, centered, and to have finite LocalDef001 scales.

The conclusion is conditional on K > 0. If every real-converted scale is zero, then K = 0 and the implication has a false antecedent, so the proposition imposes no exponential-moment conclusion on that family.
Because K > 0 is assumed before |lam| ≤ c/K, the denominator in c/K is nonzero; totalized real division does not affect this branch.
The parameter lam may be positive, negative, or zero, but must lie in the specified symmetric interval.
At lam = 0, the conclusion concerns the constant function exp(0) = 1 and bounds its integral by exp(0) = 1.
The bound uses each individual scale squared on the right, while only the admissible range for lam uses the family maximum K.
Although individual admissible scales in LocalDef002 must be nonzero and finite, their infimum LocalDef001 may equal zero and need not be attained.
The explicit finiteness hypotheses ensure that ENNReal.toReal is not applied to infinity.
No conclusion is asserted for parameters outside |lam| ≤ c/K.
The result supplies both integrability and a numerical upper bound for each individual exponential moment; it does not state a bound for a product or a sum.
ambiguities: The anonymous LocalDef001 is interpreted only through its displayed infimum definition; no additional norm identity, norm axioms, scaling law, or attainment theorem is supplied.

The supplied one-level definition of ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun refers to kernel independence without expanding that internal predicate; it is interpreted as mutual independence of the indexed functions.
The body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque beyond its supplied type and owner module, so it is interpreted as the real Bochner integral.
The dossier does not independently characterize exactly when LocalDef001 is zero or when its admissible-scale infimum is attained.
No preferred numerical values for the existential constants c and C are specified.
